questions.q: Why does this capstone use permanent tables for raw.*, staging.*, and marts.*, instead of transient?
options: Driftwood's raw data isn't reliably reproducible from the source system later, so full Time Travel + Fail-safe recovery matters throughout the project, not just on the marts
Snowflake requires all data warehouse tables to be permanent by default
Transient tables cannot be queried by dbt
Permanent tables are always cheaper than transient tables
questions.explain: Unlike a reload-from-source staging table (the classic TRANSIENT case), Driftwood's raw exports are the only copy once the source file is gone, justifying permanent tables everywhere.

questions.q: What does AT (OFFSET => -7200) do when querying a table?
options: Queries the table as it existed 2 hours (7200 seconds) in the past, using Time Travel
Deletes the last 7200 rows from the table
Offsets the table's column order by 7200 positions
Schedules a query to run 7200 seconds from now
questions.explain: Time Travel's AT (OFFSET => ...) syntax queries a table as it existed at a specific past point directly, in seconds offset from now.

questions.q: What's required to recover data from Fail-safe, as opposed to Time Travel?
options: Contacting Snowflake support directly -- it isn't a self-service recovery mechanism
Running UNDROP TABLE, identical to Time Travel recovery
Nothing extra -- Fail-safe recovery is fully self-service via SQL
Fail-safe data cannot be recovered under any circumstances
questions.explain: Fail-safe exists for genuine disaster recovery and requires contacting Snowflake support -- it's not a convenient undo button the way Time Travel's self-service window is.

questions.q: What does Time Travel NOT protect against, according to this lesson?
options: A corrupted source export that passed through the pipeline unnoticed -- Time Travel can restore the table to a prior state, but that prior state was also built from the same bad data
An accidental DROP TABLE
A bad dbt model overwriting a table with wrong data
Any form of data loss whatsoever
questions.explain: Time Travel protects against bad operations on correct data, not bad data arriving in the first place -- which is why load validation and dbt tests exist as a separate defense layer.

questions.q: Within what window does UNDROP TABLE actually work?
options: Only within the table's Time Travel retention window
Indefinitely, with no time limit
Only within the Fail-safe window, never during Time Travel
Only within the first 5 minutes after the DROP
questions.explain: UNDROP relies on Time Travel -- once that window passes, the data moves into the support-only Fail-safe period, and UNDROP itself no longer works.
